model_interpretation.claim: The prior one-ended progression was valid and faster than baseline, but still used a starting powf and accumulated powers along one chain. Anchoring at exponent zero (j=32) and generating the positive and negative exponents in separate geometric progressions removes terminal powf calls and limits each progression to 32 values. This tests whether the shorter, two-sided chains improve runtime or FP32 error; the controller must measure and validate this candidate.

items.subject: Reduce terminal payoff power-generation cost without changing the recurrence
items.objective: Keep the existing 64-value terminal array and backward recurrence, but replace per-node powf calls with a geometric power progression (for example, one starting power followed by multiplication by u squared). Preserve the exact j=0..63 terminal indexing and recurrence order. Measure whether the reduction in transcendental calls helps, and validate FP32 error over varied inputs before retaining it.
